properties.title: PatientWM: Towards Generalizable Clinical World Models via Unified Patient States

properties.version_basis: PDF identified by SHA-256 against assignments.json; title page read.

properties.description: Retrospective evaluation of a unified-patient-state clinical world model on MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV and three external clinical datasets against four adapted baselines.
properties.independent_study_claim: single research group; public data under data-use agreements

properties.description: Availability-aware lab, clinical-fact and frozen-waveform encoders, action encoder, bounded ordered latent history, causal Transformer residual transition with momentum target encoder, typed decoders and recursive rollout.

properties.algorithm: PatientWM causal Transformer residual transition (main MIMIC-III checkpoint)

properties.population: adult ICU and related clinical cohorts in public datasets
properties.decision: retrospective representation and factual forecasting only
properties.autonomy: not for bedside monitoring, treatment selection or autonomous simulation

properties.description: MIMIC-III ICU test split (5,337 test episodes from 3,827 subjects); subject-disjoint
MIMIC-IV test cohort with patient-disjoint split and six-hour transition unit
MIMIC-IV action-planning set of 15,951 test trajectories (13,143 decisions with non-empty recorded updates)
Held-out test evaluation on subject-disjoint MIMIC splits and three external datasets; baselines are source-inspired adaptations retrained on common tensors

assertions.rationale: Cohort-level provenance for governed public data.
Records are aligned to contiguous six-hour windows and empty windows remain in the timeline.
Chart-availability time is retained per event and only boundary-known, chart-available treatment information enters the action port.
Every observation component has an availability mask that gates fusion and loss.
Laboratory value age in windows is carried in the recursive cache and used by decoders.

assertions.rationale: Fixed grid with sparse tokens.

assertions.rationale: Acknowledged and partly modelled, not analysed.

criteria_met: Execution time and chart-availability time are both retained per event
criteria_missing: Audit of timestamp reliability across tables
assertions.rationale: Two time stamps kept, no audit.

criteria_met: Dataset-specific encoders map variables into a common state width

criteria_missing: Harmonization of units and coding across external datasets
assertions.rationale: Interface-level harmonization.
Subject-disjoint splits, labels stored only in the target window and decision-boundary action information.
No federated arrangement is described.
Availability-aware laboratory, clinical-fact and waveform encoders are ablated by modality.
A frozen pretrained waveform encoder supplies 512-dimensional embeddings with no downstream fine-tuning.
Transitions are trained against a momentum-encoder next-window latent target.

criteria_met: A momentum-updated target encoder with stopped gradient supplies the latent target
criteria_missing: An explicit collapse or rank test on the learned state
assertions.rationale: Design guard without a test.

criteria_met: Auxiliary next-window clinical-fact, laboratory and waveform-embedding heads ground the state
criteria_missing: Reconstruction of the current observation from the encoded state

Fusion uses only modalities available at each step.
A latent patient state and bounded ordered history are carried across transitions and evaluated by ablation and recursive rollout.
The implemented transition yields a point prediction and no belief distribution over the state is modelled.

criteria_met: Teacher-forced evaluation re-encodes each observed state
Free-running evaluation propagates predicted states
criteria_missing: A learned correction that fuses prediction with a new observation

Treatment identity, amount, rate, unit, route and execution evidence form typed token features.

relation_assertions.rationale: Action-conditioned latent patient-state dynamics with bounded candidate-action scoring evaluated as a behavioral surrogate, with no identified effect claim and no learned policy. BP_CONTROLLER is not met because no policy optimization or closed-loop test is reported.

Reviewer mapping: availability-aware state encoders, an action port, a learned causal-Transformer transition and a recursive rollout are described. M7 is not mapped because no effect layer is implemented and the authors disclaim causal effect estimation.

capability_assessments.rationale: Action-conditioned next-window and recursive predictions are scored against held-out records with action ablation and baseline comparison, supporting L2 (V12, V13). L3 is not assigned because the candidate-action comparison ranks a bounded set by a fixed burden score and the authors state that outcomes of unexecuted actions are unobserved and agreement is a behavioral surrogate. L4 is not assigned because no policy is learned or executed. Core membership (V11) is met by a persistent latent patient state with ordered history, learned temporal dynamics and a healthcare ICU setting.

gate_assessments.rationale: Public datasets under data-use terms, subject-disjoint splits, target-window label placement, and decision-boundary action information are described, but data.provenance (assertion:B030:0001) is partial (dataset version identifiers for every source and the released artifact/code repository URL are not reported in the PDF) and leakage controls are documented at specification stage without an executed leakage audit test.
Teacher-forced next-window prediction is scored on subject-disjoint test sets against four adapted baselines with matched inputs.
Rollouts to 96 hours are scored but no supported maximum horizon or drift reference is stated.
Action conditioning is ablated, but alternative-action evidence is a behavioral surrogate that the authors state does not reveal outcomes of unexecuted actions.

legacy_cells.B: PatientWM: Towards Generalizable Clinical World Models via Unified Patient States
legacy_cells.C: Ziwen Kan; Jie Peng; Bo Yan; Davis Hobley; Zheng Zhang; Yu Tian; Tianlong Chen; Song Wang
legacy_cells.O: ICU clinical trajectories with AKI, acidemia, ventilation and pressor events, sepsis, mortality, and laboratory-value targets
legacy_cells.S: Forecast next-window clinical events/outcomes and laboratory values from ICU patient states under supplied recorded actions; recursive forecasts are evaluated through 96 hours.
legacy_cells.X: F2 EHR / ICU event & latent patient dynamics
legacy_cells.AI: Sparse laboratory tokens; masked clinical facts; frozen waveform-derived embeddings; active-treatment records as action input
legacy_cells.AJ: Laboratory token identity/numeric-feature encoders with learned-query attention; clinical facts linear projection; frozen pretrained waveform encoder and linear projection; availability-aware multi-head attention for modality fusion
legacy_cells.AM: Learned observation query uses multi-head attention over available modality-branch states, with modality type embeddings and availability masks.
legacy_cells.AN: Availability masks exclude unavailable inputs; learned empty-modality embeddings represent absent laboratory or waveform branches, and an empty-state embedding is used when all branches are absent.
legacy_cells.AT: No explicit observation-based filtering update is described; observed states are encoded from current observations, while free-running rollout recursively reuses predicted states.
legacy_cells.BD: Treatment identity; lifecycle/exposure; amount; rate; unit; source; execution evidence; timing features
legacy_cells.BL: Contiguous six-hour windows; evaluation horizons of 6, 24, 48, and 96 hours
legacy_cells.BS: Predicted next latent patient state; clinical event/outcome probabilities; waveform embeddings; clinical-fact probabilities; laboratory-availability probabilities; normalized laboratory values
legacy_cells.BT: Typed clinical event/outcome, waveform, clinical-fact, laboratory-availability, joint laboratory-value, and queried laboratory-value readouts
legacy_cells.BU: Action-probe score combines predicted event burden and laboratory burden under a fixed scoring rule; a fixed uncertainty penalty is shared across methods.
legacy_cells.BV: Latent-state cosine alignment; waveform cosine loss; masked binary cross-entropy for clinical facts and laboratory availability; masked Smooth-L1 for observed laboratory values; residual-update regularization; recursive rollout objective
legacy_cells.BY: 5,685,029 parameters for the main MIMIC-III configuration
legacy_cells.CK: Bounded candidate actions are scored using predicted event and laboratory burdens combined by the same fixed scoring rule; agreement with the recorded action is measured by covered top-k ranking.
legacy_cells.CV: The transition target is the conditional distribution induced by the observed clinical process, explicitly not an interventional treatment-response law; the paper states it does not estimate causal treatment effects.
legacy_cells.FN: On the covered subset of bounded-candidate action comparisons, PatientWM recorded-action agreement was 0.7477 top-1 and 0.9126 top-2. Candidate coverage was 0.5573 in 13,143 eligible non-empty-update decisions, from 15,951 test trajectories. Agreement is a clinician-behavior surrogate, not a treatment-benefit estimate.
legacy_cells.FR: The bounded candidate set and fixed scoring rule produce recorded-action agreement on covered decisions. This supports alternative-action comparison, not identified treatment effects, benefit over clinician care, prospective optimization or deployment. Candidate coverage and conditional top-k agreement must be reported together.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M4 Action service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M6 Rollout service; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Pass the paper’s specified action and time context explicitly into the state-transition interface; preserve the boundary between predictive action sensitivity and identified intervention effects.
legacy_cells.FX: Complete extracted PDF text, pp. 1–28: title/abstract, introduction and related work (pp. 1–2); methods (pp. 3–5); experiments/results and displayed tables (pp. 5–10); conclusion, AI-use and ethics statements (p. 10); references (pp. 11–13); dataset construction, action ledger and governance (pp. 14–15); architecture, decoders, training, hyperparameters and tensor contract (pp. 15–20); comparison methods and evaluation protocols (pp. 21–23); supplementary results and action-planning boundary (pp. 24–27); reproducibility/artifacts (pp. 27–28). No separate limitations section appears; the action-planning surrogate boundary and intended-use restrictions were read. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I were left untouched for parent preservation. The paper demonstrates state/action-conditioned factual prediction and recursive rollout; the bounded candidate action probe reports agreement with recorded clinician behavior, not causal treatment effects, counterfactual correctness, treatment optimality, or prospective benefit. Authors describe planning support (AA), but experimental action ranking is not evidence of autonomous clinical decision support. No separate limitations heading was present. Evidence QA: 51/62 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (82.3%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 58 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 4 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: Targeted 2026-11-22 review resolved remaining visual-inventory and bibliography-entry gaps on the same hash-pinned PDF. Prior text/visual work is reused with original attribution; details and actual new page receipts are in verification.json. Bibliographies were read as entries only; cited full texts and external videos/code were not inspected.
Figures 3–6 rechecked against supplementary Tables 12–17. Primary performance rows remain point estimates; p26 separately gives a patient-cluster interval for candidate coverage.
Baselines are source-inspired adaptations retrained by the authors on a common interface, so metric rows describe the adapted baselines and not the cited systems.
No confidence intervals, seeds or significance tests were found for Tables 1 to 5, so none are recorded.
The release claim is stated in the ethics paragraph, no repository location was found in the text read, and release features are not verified.
Legacy cells were read from the root workbook row (read only). Unlisted columns remain imported-only. Saved API drafts for B030 were not opened.
Schema validity and quote occurrence do not establish semantic correctness. One reviewer pass; no independent human review.
notes: Clinical world model built around a unified latent patient state, with availability-aware encoders, an action port from boundary-active treatments, a bounded ordered state-action history, a causal-Transformer residual transition with momentum-encoder target and typed decoders. Evaluated retrospectively on subject-disjoint MIMIC splits, label-efficient adaptation and three external datasets against four adapted baselines. L2 supported by action and history ablations and recursive rollouts. L3 and L4 not adopted since candidate-action scoring is a behavioral surrogate and no policy is executed. Source points: baselines are the authors' adaptations, no intervals for primary performance tables (p26 separately reports a patient-cluster interval for candidate coverage), absolute scores low on Common Event-7 (AUPRC under 0.1 on MIMIC-III), no calibration audit, and an AI-assisted manuscript disclosure.
